verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The market empties out and the pigeons take the square.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Grey wings settle on spilled rice—
someone's dinner, someone's loss,
another day of getting by

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A shutter clatters half-down,
the seller counting coins by streetlight,
tomorrow already loading on the cart.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Cold hands, warm bread wrapped in paper—
he hands it to the boy who has no coins,
says nothing, turns back to the dark.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The steam rises once, then thins to nothing—
the boy walks on, the paper warm against his chest,
morning still hours away.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Somewhere a kettle starts to sing—
a window catches, gold, then dims,
the street keeps none of it for long

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
He counts his change beneath a lamp that flickers,
five coins for bread, one held back for luck—
the boy has already turned the corner

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The lamp gives up, the corner empties out—
somewhere a door unlatches for no one,
luck spends itself before the morning comes

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Frost blooms quiet on the sill—
someone's breath still fogs the glass
though the room has long gone empty

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
A crow lands where the footprints end—
it studies what the frost has kept,
then lifts, unbothered, into gray

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The gray accepts it without a seam—
somewhere a bell forgets to ring,
the hour arrives with nothing to announce

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I sweep the step though no one's come—
the broom finds only what the wind left,
and calls that clean enough

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A kettle ticks itself back to silence—
someone once counted the whistles
before the counting mattered less than tea

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
steam finds the window and forgets its shape—
outside, the same bare tree keeps score
of winters no one asked it to remember

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the tree's tally blurs in morning frost—
a sparrow lands where zero would have been
and does not care what number it disturbs

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the sparrow lifts before the frost can name it—
gone is easier than counted,
and the branch forgets to mind
